summary: Mehamn Airport is a small regional airport situated on the Nordkinn Peninsula in Finnmark, northern Norway, serving the remote fishing village of Mehamn in Nordkapp Municipality. The peninsula is the northernmost point of mainland Europe, making the airport one of the most northerly in mainland Norway. The short runway and challenging coastal terrain make it a vital lifeline for the isolated local community.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly to Mehamn Airport?
A: Widerøe operates regular scheduled flights, typically using Dash 8 turboprop aircraft suited to the short runway.

Q: Where is Mehamn located?
A: Mehamn is on the Nordkinn Peninsula in Finnmark county, northern Norway, near the North Cape region.

Q: How long is the runway at Mehamn?
A: The runway is relatively short, approximately 900 meters, which limits aircraft size and requires skilled operations in variable Arctic weather.

Q: When is the best time to visit Mehamn?
A: Summer (June to August) offers the midnight sun and milder weather, while winter provides opportunities to see the northern lights, though conditions can be harsh.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few kilometers from Mehamn village center, making taxi or pre-arranged transport quick and straightforward. Car rental availability is limited, so booking in advance is recommended. Many visitors combine a flight to Mehamn with onward ferry connections along the coast.
local_tip: If traveling in winter, build in a buffer day or two into your itinerary, as fog, snow, and strong coastal winds can cause flight cancellations at short notice, even when conditions at your origin airport appear fine.
